name: Three rules for making a randomised/Euclidean sequencer sound intentional: constrain (scale, octave range, pitches pulled close, phrase length), repeat (global randomness to zero, reset per-step random, restart points so the phrase retriggers each bar), and simplify (about three pitches, fewer pulses, complexity from layering simple parts), then add hand-made variations on chosen cycles and random pitch options on only the last few notes
goal: Fix a generative patch that sounds aimlessly random. Rule 1, constrain: set a scale (e.g. minor), reduce octave range/voicing, and pull spread-out notes into closer octaves; limit phrase length. Rule 2, repetition creates anticipation: turn global continuous randomisation to zero, reset any per-step randomisation (use only a little, on a couple of notes), and set a restart point so the pitch and trigger lists start together each bar, so the ear can remember the hook. Rule 3, less is more: cut to about three pitches and fewer pulses; get complexity from several simple layers, not one complex one. Then add intentional variation: in a later cycle (e.g. bar 2) add extra notes, copy that variation to other cycles, move start points, push one note up an octave or add a roll; for controlled surprise, give only the last four notes extra pitch options. Apply the same rules to each part. Complements our probability/seeded generative skills as the taming pass.

source.title: Torso T1: The 3 Rules That Make Generative Sequencing Musical

prerequisites: Any generative or Euclidean step sequencer or DAW, or Polyrhythm Studio lanes / JS scheduler with scale quantiser, per-step random amounts, and a phrase reset (implementation note)

inputs.name: parts
inputs.description: Generative parts currently playing (four in the video)

outputs.name: tamed_parts
outputs.description: Constrained, repeating, simplified parts with deliberate variations

outputs.name: variation_map
outputs.description: Which cycles and notes carry variation or randomness

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
These are taste rules; break them deliberately once the hook works.
Device controls are specific to the presenter's sequencer; apply the same moves in any sequencer. Membership promotion dropped.

steps.action: Solo one part. Set a scale, reduce octave range, and move notes into nearby octaves.
steps.expect: Still varied, but boxed into a coherent register

steps.action: Set global continuous randomisation to zero and reset per-step random amounts on all steps.
steps.expect: The line repeats and sounds intentional

steps.action: Add a restart point so pitch and trigger cycles realign at the start of every bar.
steps.expect: A clear start point; the motif is recognisable

steps.action: Reduce to about three pitches and fewer pulses; optionally add a second restart point.
Pick a cycle (e.g. bar 2) and hand-add notes; copy that variation to other cycles, change start points, raise one note an octave, add a roll.
Give only the last few notes (e.g. last four) extra pitch options or randomisation.
steps.expect: Small surprises at phrase ends while the hook stays fixed

steps.action: Repeat rules 1–3 for each other part and listen to them together.

verification: With global random at zero and a restart each bar, the part is identical on consecutive bars except at the chosen variation notes.
All notes fall within the chosen scale and the reduced octave range.
Only the targeted last notes change pitch from cycle to cycle.
